questions.question: Which book of the Bible records the creation of the world?
questions.explanation: The creation account is found in Genesis.

questions.question: Who created the heavens and the earth?
questions.explanation: Genesis begins by declaring that God created everything.

questions.question: After creating the world, how did God describe His creation?
questions.explanation: God saw all He had made and declared it very good.

questions.question: What did God create on the first day?
questions.explanation: Light was created on the first day.

questions.question: On which day were the sun, moon and stars created?
questions.explanation: The heavenly lights were created on the fourth day.

questions.question: On which day did God create human beings?
questions.explanation: Human beings were created on the sixth day.

questions.question: What did God do on the seventh day?
questions.explanation: God rested from His work on the seventh day.

questions.question: How many days did God spend creating the world?
questions.explanation: Creation took six days.

questions.question: What was special about the seventh day?
answers: It was blessed and made holy
questions.explanation: God blessed and sanctified the seventh day.

questions.question: What was the name of the garden where God placed Adam?
questions.explanation: God placed Adam in the Garden of Eden.

questions.question: Who was the first man created by God?
questions.explanation: Adam was the first man created by God.

questions.question: What responsibility did God give Adam in the garden?
questions.explanation: Adam was instructed to work and take care of the garden.

questions.question: Why did God create Eve?
questions.explanation: God created Eve because it was not good for Adam to be alone.

questions.question: From what part of Adam did God create Eve?
questions.explanation: God created Eve from one of Adam's ribs.

questions.question: What did Adam say when he first saw Eve?
answers: This is now bone of my bones
questions.explanation: Adam recognized Eve as part of himself.

questions.question: Which creature tempted Eve in the garden?
questions.explanation: The serpent tempted Eve to disobey God.

questions.question: Which tree were Adam and Eve forbidden to eat from?
answers: Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil
questions.explanation: God commanded them not to eat from that tree.

questions.question: What happened immediately after Adam and Eve ate the fruit?
questions.explanation: They became aware of their nakedness after disobeying God.

questions.question: Why were Adam and Eve sent out of the Garden of Eden?
questions.explanation: Their disobedience brought consequences.

questions.question: Who guarded the entrance to the Garden of Eden?
questions.explanation: Cherubim guarded the way to the Tree of Life.

questions.question: What tree was protected after Adam and Eve left Eden?
questions.explanation: The Tree of Life was guarded after their expulsion.

questions.question: Who were the first two sons of Adam and Eve mentioned in the Bible?
questions.explanation: Cain and Abel were the first brothers mentioned in Scripture.

questions.question: What work did Cain do?
questions.explanation: Cain worked the soil as a farmer.

questions.question: What animals did Abel care for?
questions.explanation: Abel was a keeper of sheep.

questions.question: Who brought an offering from his flock?
questions.explanation: Abel brought the best portions from his flock.

questions.question: Whose offering did God look upon with favor?
questions.explanation: God looked with favor on Abel and his offering.

questions.question: How did Cain react when his offering was not favored?
questions.explanation: Cain became very angry and downcast.

questions.question: What sin led Cain to attack Abel?
questions.explanation: Jealousy and anger led Cain to sin.

questions.question: Where did Cain kill Abel?
questions.explanation: Cain attacked Abel while they were in the field.

questions.question: After the murder, what did God ask Cain?
questions.explanation: God asked Cain about Abel's whereabouts.

questions.question: What punishment did Cain receive?
questions.explanation: Cain was sentenced to be a restless wanderer.

questions.question: What special sign did God place on Cain?
questions.explanation: God marked Cain so others would not kill him.

questions.question: What lesson can be learned from Cain and Abel's story?
questions.explanation: Unchecked jealousy and anger can lead to serious sin.

questions.question: Why did God decide to judge the world in Noah's time?
answers: The earth was filled with wickedness
questions.explanation: God saw that the earth was full of evil.

questions.question: Who found favor in the eyes of the Lord?
questions.explanation: Noah was righteous among the people of his generation.

questions.question: What made Noah different from many people of his time?
answers: He was the oldest man alive
questions.explanation: Noah faithfully followed God.

questions.question: What did God tell Noah to build?
questions.explanation: God instructed Noah to build an ark.

questions.question: Why was Noah told to build the ark?
questions.explanation: The ark would preserve life during the flood.

questions.question: How did Noah respond to God's instructions?
questions.explanation: Noah did everything God commanded him to do.

questions.question: How long did it rain during the flood?
questions.explanation: Rain fell for forty days and forty nights.

questions.question: Who entered the ark before the flood began?
questions.explanation: Those God chose to preserve entered the ark.

questions.question: What did the dove bring back to Noah?
questions.explanation: The olive leaf showed that the waters were receding.

questions.question: What sign did God give as a reminder of His covenant?
questions.explanation: The rainbow became the sign of God's covenant.

questions.question: What did God promise after the flood?
answers: Never again to destroy the earth by flood
questions.explanation: God promised never again to destroy the earth by flood.

questions.question: What lesson is most clearly taught by Noah's story?
answers: Animals are more important than people
questions.explanation: Noah's obedience and faithfulness are central themes of the story.

questions.question: How many languages did people speak after the flood?
questions.explanation: The Bible says the whole world had one language.

questions.question: What made communication easy among the people?
questions.explanation: Everyone spoke the same language.

questions.question: What did the people decide to do together?
questions.explanation: They decided to build a city together.

questions.question: What famous structure did the people begin to build?
questions.explanation: The people built a tower later known as the Tower of Babel.

questions.question: Why did the people want to build the tower?
answers: To make a name for themselves
questions.explanation: They wanted fame and recognition for themselves.

questions.question: What attitude motivated the builders?
questions.explanation: The builders were motivated by pride and self-importance.

questions.question: How did God stop the building of the tower?
answers: He destroyed the city with fire
questions.explanation: God confused their language so they could not cooperate.

questions.question: What happened after the people's language was confused?
answers: They could not understand one another
questions.explanation: The people could no longer communicate effectively.

questions.question: What does the name Babel relate to in the story?
questions.explanation: Babel is associated with the confusion of languages.

questions.question: What happened to the people after the Tower of Babel?
questions.explanation: The people spread throughout the earth.

questions.question: Why did people spread into different regions?
questions.explanation: Language barriers caused people to separate.

questions.question: What is the main message of the Tower of Babel story?
answers: God opposes human pride and disobedience
questions.explanation: The story highlights God's authority and the danger of pride.

questions.question: What was Abraham's name before God changed it?
questions.explanation: Abraham was originally called Abram.

questions.question: What did God tell Abram to do?
questions.explanation: God called Abram to leave his homeland and follow Him.

questions.question: How did Abram respond to God's call?
questions.explanation: Abram obeyed God's instruction and left his homeland.

questions.question: What did God compare Abraham's descendants to?
questions.explanation: God promised descendants as numerous as the stars.

questions.question: What land did God promise Abraham?
questions.explanation: God promised Abraham the land of Canaan.

questions.question: What was Abraham known for?
questions.explanation: Abraham is remembered as a man of faith.

questions.question: Who was Lot to Abraham?
questions.explanation: Lot was Abraham's nephew.

questions.question: Why did Abraham and Lot separate?
questions.explanation: Their livestock increased and the land could not support both groups together.

questions.question: What lesson is taught by Abraham's treatment of Lot?
questions.explanation: Abraham demonstrated wisdom and peacemaking.

questions.question: What was the name of Abraham's promised son?
questions.explanation: God promised Abraham and Sarah a son named Isaac.

questions.question: Who was Isaac's mother?
questions.explanation: Sarah gave birth to Isaac in her old age.

questions.question: What does the name Isaac mean?
questions.explanation: Isaac means 'he laughs,' reflecting Sarah's joy.

questions.question: Whose son was Joseph?
questions.explanation: Joseph was one of Jacob's sons.

questions.question: Why did Joseph's brothers become jealous of him?
answers: His dreams suggested he would rule over them
questions.explanation: Joseph's dreams caused jealousy among his brothers.

questions.question: How many brothers did Joseph have?
questions.explanation: Joseph had eleven brothers, making twelve sons of Jacob.

questions.question: What did Joseph's brothers do to him?
questions.explanation: Joseph was sold to traders heading to Egypt.

questions.question: To which country was Joseph taken?
questions.explanation: Joseph was taken to Egypt as a slave.

questions.question: What character flaw caused Joseph's brothers to betray him?
questions.explanation: Their jealousy led them to commit a terrible act.

questions.question: Why was Joseph sent to prison?
questions.explanation: Joseph was imprisoned because of a false accusation.

questions.question: Who remained with Joseph during his suffering?
questions.explanation: God was with Joseph even in prison.

questions.question: What lesson can be learned from Joseph's prison experience?
answers: Give up when life is hard
questions.explanation: Joseph trusted God even in hardship.

questions.question: Who had the dreams that Joseph interpreted?
questions.explanation: Joseph interpreted Pharaoh's dreams.

questions.question: What did Pharaoh appoint Joseph to become?
questions.explanation: Joseph became second in command in Egypt.

questions.question: What gift from God helped Joseph rise to power?
questions.explanation: God gave Joseph wisdom to interpret dreams.

questions.question: Where were the Israelites living when Moses was born?
questions.explanation: The Israelites were living in Egypt during Moses' birth.

questions.question: How did Moses' mother protect him?
answers: She hid him in a basket
She hid him in a cave
questions.explanation: Moses was placed in a basket on the Nile River.

questions.question: Who found Moses in the basket?
questions.explanation: Pharaoh's daughter discovered Moses in the Nile.

questions.question: Where did God speak to Moses from?
questions.explanation: God spoke to Moses through the burning bush.

questions.question: What special thing happened to the bush?
questions.explanation: The bush remained intact while burning.

questions.question: What mission did God give Moses?
answers: Lead the Israelites out of slavery
questions.explanation: God called Moses to deliver Israel.

questions.question: Why did God send plagues upon Egypt?
answers: Because Pharaoh refused to let Israel go
questions.explanation: The plagues came because Pharaoh resisted God's command.

questions.question: How many plagues were sent upon Egypt?
questions.explanation: God sent ten plagues in total.

questions.question: What finally caused Pharaoh to let the Israelites go?
questions.explanation: After the final plague, Pharaoh released Israel.

questions.question: What body of water did the Israelites cross?
questions.explanation: God parted the Red Sea for Israel.

questions.question: How did the Israelites cross the sea?
questions.explanation: The sea was divided and the people crossed on dry ground.

questions.question: What lesson is most clearly taught by the Red Sea crossing?
questions.explanation: The Red Sea demonstrates God's saving power.

questions.question: Who became Israel's leader after Moses?
questions.explanation: Joshua succeeded Moses as leader of Israel.

questions.question: What land was Joshua leading the Israelites into?
questions.explanation: Joshua led Israel into the Promised Land.

questions.question: What quality was Joshua especially encouraged to have?
questions.explanation: God encouraged Joshua to be courageous.

questions.question: Which city did Joshua send spies to investigate?
questions.explanation: The spies were sent to Jericho.

questions.question: Who helped the spies escape?
questions.explanation: Rahab hid and protected the spies.

questions.question: Why did Rahab help the spies?
questions.explanation: Rahab believed that God was with Israel.

questions.question: Which river did the Israelites cross under Joshua's leadership?
questions.explanation: Israel crossed the Jordan River into the Promised Land.

questions.question: What sacred object did the priests carry?
questions.explanation: The priests carried the Ark of the Covenant.

questions.question: What did the crossing of the Jordan demonstrate?
questions.explanation: The miracle showed God's presence with Israel.

questions.question: What surrounded the city of Jericho?
questions.explanation: Jericho was protected by strong walls.

questions.question: How many days did Israel march around Jericho before the walls fell?
questions.explanation: The walls fell on the seventh day.

questions.question: What lesson is taught by the fall of Jericho?
questions.explanation: Israel's victory came because they obeyed God's instructions.

questions.question: Who announced the birth of Samson?
questions.explanation: An angel announced Samson's birth.

questions.question: What special vow was Samson to follow?
questions.explanation: Samson was dedicated to God as a Nazirite.

questions.question: Which enemies were oppressing Israel during Samson's time?
questions.explanation: The Philistines ruled over Israel during Samson's time.

questions.question: What was Samson famous for?
questions.explanation: Samson was known for his extraordinary strength.

questions.question: What animal did Samson kill with his bare hands?
questions.explanation: Samson killed a lion through God's strength.

questions.question: Who gave Samson his strength?
questions.explanation: Samson's strength came from God.

questions.question: Who tried to discover the secret of Samson's strength?
questions.explanation: Delilah was used by the Philistines.

questions.question: What was connected to Samson's Nazirite vow?
questions.explanation: His hair symbolized his Nazirite dedication.

questions.question: What mistake did Samson make?
questions.explanation: Samson revealed a secret he should have protected.

questions.question: What happened to Samson's hair while he was imprisoned?
questions.explanation: Samson's hair grew again while in prison.

questions.question: What did Samson do during the Philistine celebration?
questions.explanation: Samson brought down the Philistine temple.

questions.question: What lesson can be learned from Samson's life?
answers: God can still use people who return to Him
questions.explanation: Samson's story shows both the consequences of failure and God's mercy.

questions.question: What was David's occupation before becoming king?
questions.explanation: David cared for his father's sheep.

questions.question: Who was David's father?
questions.explanation: David was the son of Jesse.

questions.question: Where did David spend much of his youth?
questions.explanation: David spent his youth as a shepherd.

questions.question: Who was Goliath?
questions.explanation: Goliath was a giant warrior from Philistia.

questions.question: Which army did Goliath belong to?
questions.explanation: Goliath fought for the Philistines.

questions.question: How did the Israelite soldiers react to Goliath?
questions.explanation: The soldiers were terrified of Goliath.

questions.question: What weapon did David use against Goliath?
questions.explanation: David used a sling and a stone.

questions.question: Why was David confident before the battle?
questions.explanation: David's confidence came from faith in God.

questions.question: What happened after the stone hit Goliath?
questions.explanation: The stone struck Goliath and he fell.

questions.question: What was the main reason for David's victory?
questions.explanation: David trusted God rather than his own strength.

questions.question: What lesson can be learned from David's story?
questions.explanation: David's story teaches trust in God.

questions.question: What does David's story teach about God?
answers: God helps those who trust Him
questions.explanation: God worked through David because of his faith.

questions.question: To which country was Daniel taken?
questions.explanation: Daniel was taken captive to Babylon.

questions.question: What did Daniel refuse to do?
answers: Defile himself with the king's food
questions.explanation: Daniel remained faithful to God's laws.

questions.question: What did God give Daniel?
questions.explanation: God blessed Daniel with wisdom and knowledge.

questions.question: Who refused to worship the golden image?
questions.explanation: Daniel's three friends remained faithful to God.

questions.question: What punishment did they receive?
questions.explanation: They were thrown into a blazing furnace.

questions.question: What happened to the three men in the furnace?
questions.explanation: God protected them from the fire.

questions.question: Which king saw the writing on the wall?
questions.explanation: Belshazzar saw the mysterious writing.

questions.question: Who interpreted the writing?
questions.explanation: God gave Daniel the interpretation.

questions.question: What did the writing on the wall announce?
questions.explanation: The message announced the fall of Belshazzar's kingdom.

questions.question: Why was Daniel thrown into the lions' den?
answers: He disobeyed the king in battle
questions.explanation: Daniel would not stop praying to God.

questions.question: What happened to the lions?
questions.explanation: God protected Daniel from the lions.

questions.question: What lesson is most clearly taught by Daniel's life?
answers: Remain faithful to God in every circumstance
questions.explanation: Daniel's life is an example of faithfulness and trust in God.

questions.question: What city did God tell Jonah to visit?
questions.explanation: God commanded Jonah to go to Nineveh.

questions.question: How did Jonah respond to God's command at first?
questions.explanation: Jonah tried to flee from God's assignment.

questions.question: What lesson is learned from Jonah's decision to flee?
questions.explanation: Jonah discovered that God's plans cannot be avoided.

questions.question: What happened while Jonah was on the ship?
questions.explanation: God sent a powerful storm.

questions.question: Who was identified as the cause of the storm?
questions.explanation: Jonah admitted he was running from God.

questions.question: How was the storm stopped?
answers: Jonah was thrown into the sea
questions.explanation: The sea became calm after Jonah was thrown overboard.

questions.question: What happened to Jonah after he was thrown into the sea?
questions.explanation: God provided a great fish to save Jonah.

questions.question: How long was Jonah inside the fish?
questions.explanation: Jonah spent three days and three nights in the fish.

questions.question: What did the fish eventually do?
questions.explanation: God commanded the fish to release Jonah.

questions.question: What did Jonah do after leaving the fish?
questions.explanation: Jonah finally obeyed God's command.

questions.question: How did the people of Nineveh respond to Jonah's message?
questions.explanation: The people turned from their evil ways.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of Jonah's story?
answers: God is merciful to those who repent
questions.explanation: Jonah's story highlights God's mercy, forgiveness, and desire for repentance.

questions.question: Which angel appeared to Mary?
questions.explanation: The angel Gabriel delivered God's message to Mary.

questions.question: What was Mary told she would give birth to?
questions.explanation: Gabriel announced the birth of Jesus.

questions.question: How did Mary respond to God's message?
questions.explanation: Mary humbly accepted God's will.

questions.question: In which town was Jesus born?
questions.explanation: Jesus was born in Bethlehem.

questions.question: Where was baby Jesus laid after His birth?
questions.explanation: Jesus was laid in a manger.

questions.question: Why was Jesus laid in a manger?
questions.explanation: There was no room available for them.

questions.question: Who first received the angelic announcement of Jesus' birth?
questions.explanation: The angels appeared to shepherds in the fields.

questions.question: What did the angels announce?
questions.explanation: The angels proclaimed the birth of Jesus.

questions.question: How did the shepherds respond to the angel's message?
answers: They went quickly to see Jesus
questions.explanation: The shepherds immediately went to Bethlehem.

questions.question: What guided the wise men to Jesus?
questions.explanation: The wise men followed a star.

questions.question: Which gift was brought by the wise men?
questions.explanation: Gold was one of the gifts presented to Jesus.

questions.question: Why did the wise men come to see Jesus?
questions.explanation: The wise men came to worship Jesus.

questions.question: Where did Jesus turn water into wine?
questions.explanation: The miracle took place at a wedding in Cana.

questions.question: What did Jesus transform into wine?
questions.explanation: Jesus turned water into wine.

questions.question: What did this miracle reveal about Jesus?
questions.explanation: The miracle demonstrated Jesus' divine authority.

questions.question: What happened while Jesus and His disciples were on the lake?
questions.explanation: A powerful storm threatened the boat.

questions.question: How did Jesus stop the storm?
answers: He rebuked the wind and waves
questions.explanation: Jesus commanded nature and it obeyed.

questions.question: What does this miracle teach?
questions.explanation: The miracle reveals Jesus' power over creation.

questions.question: How many loaves were used in the miracle?
questions.explanation: Jesus used five loaves of bread.

questions.question: How many fish were available?
questions.explanation: Two fish were part of the meal.

questions.question: What does this miracle demonstrate?
answers: Only rich people can help others
questions.explanation: Jesus showed compassion and provision.

questions.question: How did Jesus reach the disciples' boat?
questions.explanation: Jesus walked on the water.

questions.question: Which disciple stepped out of the boat?
questions.explanation: Peter walked toward Jesus on the water.

questions.question: What lesson is emphasized in this miracle?
answers: Keep your faith focused on Jesus
questions.explanation: Peter succeeded when he trusted Jesus.

questions.question: Who helped the injured man?
questions.explanation: The Samaritan showed compassion and helped the injured man.

questions.question: What happened to the man on the road?
questions.explanation: Robbers attacked and injured the traveler.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the Good Samaritan?
questions.explanation: Jesus taught us to show mercy and love to others.

questions.question: How many sheep were left behind while the shepherd searched?
questions.explanation: The shepherd left ninety-nine sheep to find one lost sheep.

questions.question: What did the shepherd do when he found the lost sheep?
questions.explanation: The shepherd celebrated when the lost sheep was found.

questions.question: What does the lost sheep represent?
answers: A person who has wandered away from God
questions.explanation: The lost sheep symbolizes someone who needs God's care.

questions.question: What did the younger son do with his inheritance?
questions.explanation: The son wasted his inheritance through reckless living.

questions.question: What happened when the son returned home?
questions.explanation: The father forgave and welcomed his son.

questions.question: What is the main message of the Prodigal Son?
questions.explanation: The story reveals God's love and forgiveness.

questions.question: Who scattered the seed in the parable?
questions.explanation: The sower spread seed on different soils.

questions.question: Which soil produced a harvest?
questions.explanation: Good soil produced an abundant harvest.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the Parable of the Sower?
answers: People respond differently to God's Word
Seeds are more important than people
questions.explanation: The parable teaches about receiving and obeying God's Word.

questions.question: Who shared the Last Supper with Jesus?
questions.explanation: Jesus shared the meal with His disciples.

questions.question: What did Jesus use to symbolize His body?
questions.explanation: Jesus broke bread and said it represented His body.

questions.question: Why did Jesus tell His disciples to remember this meal?
questions.explanation: The meal reminds believers of Jesus' sacrifice.

questions.question: Where did Jesus pray before His arrest?
questions.explanation: Jesus prayed in Gethsemane.

questions.question: What did Jesus choose in His prayer?
questions.explanation: Jesus submitted Himself to God's will.

questions.question: What lesson does Gethsemane teach?
answers: Obey God's will even when it is difficult
questions.explanation: Jesus showed complete obedience to God.

questions.question: What form of execution did Jesus suffer?
questions.explanation: Jesus was crucified on a cross.

questions.question: Why did Jesus give His life?
questions.explanation: Jesus died as a sacrifice for sin.

questions.question: What does the crucifixion demonstrate most clearly?
questions.explanation: Jesus' death reveals God's love and salvation.

questions.question: Who placed Jesus' body in the tomb?
questions.explanation: Joseph of Arimathea provided the tomb.

questions.question: What was rolled in front of the tomb?
questions.explanation: A large stone sealed the tomb.

questions.question: What event does the burial lead directly into?
questions.explanation: The next major event is Jesus' resurrection.

questions.question: On which day did Jesus rise from the dead?
questions.explanation: Jesus rose on the third day after His burial.

questions.question: What did the women find when they arrived at the tomb?
questions.explanation: The tomb was empty because Jesus had risen.

questions.question: What does the empty tomb prove?
questions.explanation: The empty tomb points to Jesus' resurrection.

questions.question: Who spoke to the women at the tomb?
questions.explanation: Angels announced the resurrection.

questions.question: What message did the angels give?
questions.explanation: The angels declared that Jesus had risen.

questions.question: How did the women respond?
questions.explanation: The women obeyed and told the disciples.

questions.question: To whom did Jesus appear after His resurrection?
questions.explanation: Jesus appeared to many witnesses.

questions.question: Which woman was among the first to see the risen Jesus?
questions.explanation: Mary Magdalene was among the first witnesses.

questions.question: Why were Jesus' appearances important?
questions.explanation: The appearances confirmed the reality of the resurrection.

questions.question: What mission did Jesus give His followers?
questions.explanation: Jesus commanded His followers to make disciples.

questions.question: What did Jesus tell believers to do in addition to making disciples?
questions.explanation: The Great Commission includes baptizing and teaching.

questions.question: What is the main message of the Great Commission?
answers: Share the Gospel with the world
questions.explanation: Jesus called His followers to spread His message everywhere.

questions.question: What happened on the Day of Pentecost?
answers: The Holy Spirit came upon believers
questions.explanation: The Holy Spirit came upon the disciples at Pentecost.

questions.question: Why did the Holy Spirit come upon the disciples?
answers: To help them preach the Gospel
questions.explanation: The Holy Spirit empowered believers to witness boldly.

questions.question: What is Pentecost often called?
questions.explanation: Many Christians consider Pentecost the beginning of the Church.

questions.question: Who preached to the crowd at Pentecost?
questions.explanation: Peter delivered the first major sermon of the Church.

questions.question: How did many people respond to Peter's message?
questions.explanation: Many accepted the Gospel and were baptized.

questions.question: What helped Peter preach boldly?
questions.explanation: The Holy Spirit empowered Peter's preaching.

questions.question: What did the early believers devote themselves to?
questions.explanation: Prayer and teaching were central to the early Church.

questions.question: How did believers treat one another?
answers: They helped and shared with each other
questions.explanation: The believers cared for each other's needs.

questions.question: What was one result of the believers' unity?
questions.explanation: Their love and unity attracted more believers.

questions.question: Who is known as the first Christian martyr?
questions.explanation: Stephen was the first Christian martyr recorded in Acts.

questions.question: What was Stephen preaching about?
questions.explanation: Stephen boldly testified about Jesus.

questions.question: What lesson can be learned from Stephen's life?
answers: Remain faithful to Jesus regardless of opposition
questions.explanation: Stephen is remembered for unwavering faith and courage.

questions.question: What was Paul's name before he became a follower of Jesus?
questions.explanation: Paul was originally known as Saul.

questions.question: Where was Saul traveling when Jesus appeared to him?
questions.explanation: Jesus appeared to Saul on the road to Damascus.

questions.question: What lesson does Saul's conversion teach?
questions.explanation: Paul's story shows God's power to transform lives.

questions.question: What was Paul's main mission?
questions.explanation: Paul traveled to share the message of Jesus.

questions.question: What did Paul establish in many cities?
questions.explanation: Paul helped start many churches.

questions.question: Why did Paul travel so much?
questions.explanation: Paul's mission was to tell others about Jesus.

questions.question: What are Paul's letters commonly called?
questions.explanation: Paul's letters are known as Epistles.

questions.question: Why did Paul write letters?
questions.explanation: Paul wrote to strengthen churches in faith.

questions.question: Why are Paul's letters important today?
answers: They teach Christian faith and living
questions.explanation: Paul's letters continue to guide Christians today.

questions.question: What challenge did Paul face during his ministry?
questions.explanation: Paul faced many hardships while serving God.

questions.question: How did Paul respond to difficulties?
questions.explanation: Paul continued serving Jesus despite hardship.

questions.question: What lesson can be learned from Paul's life?
answers: Remain faithful to God until the end
Faith is only for easy times
questions.explanation: Paul's life teaches perseverance and faithfulness.
